UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Case No. 1:26-cv-02331
V.
KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED
CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,
Defendants.
/
[PROPOSED| ORDER A
This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff's Rule 54(b) Motion to Reconsider ECF No.
108 as to ECF No. 103 (ECF No.
_). Upon consideration of the Motion, the Memorandum in
Support, any response and reply, and the record, it is hereby
ORDERED that the Motion is GRANTED to the extent stated in this Order. The Order
signed October 29, 2026 and entered October 30, 2026 (ECF No. 108) is MODIFIED insofar as it
denied Plaintiff's Motion for Entry of a Scheduling Order and, as Necessary, an Initial Pretrial
Conference (ECF No. 103). This Order acts on ECF No. 103. It does not reconsider the disposition
of ECF No. 105 in ECF No. 108; and it is
FURTHER ORDERED that a scheduling conference under Federal Rule of Civil
Procedure 16(b)(1)(B) and Local Civil Rule 16(B) is set for
_ 2026, at
1

_.m., before the undersigned, by the means directed by the Court. That date is within twenty-one
(21) days after entry of this Order; and it is
FURTHER ORDERED that, under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 26(f)(1), 26(f)(2), and
26(f)(4) and Local Civil Rule 26(A)(1), the intervals for the parties' conference and written report
are shortened as follows. Counsel of record and all unrepresented parties who have appeared shall
confer as Rule 26(f) requires on or before
→ 2026, a date no later than seven (7)
days before the scheduling conference. They shall file a written report under Rules 26(f)(2) and
26(f)(3) on or before
→ 2026, a date no later than three (3) days before the
scheduling conference. Each date falls after entry of this Order. The report shall state the parties'
agreed proposals and each party's separately attributed position on any matter not agreed,
including any party's position that initial disclosures or discovery should be deferred pending
disposition of the pending motions to dismiss (ECF Nos. 10, 21, 45); and it is
FURTHER ORDERED that a conference among the parties and a written report completed
before entry of this Order that satisfy Rules 26(f)(2) and 26(f)(3) satisfy the preceding paragraph.
No party is required to repeat a conference or report already completed. The parties shall file any
supplement necessary to address the matters identified in the preceding paragraph on or before the
report date set above; and it is
FURTHER ORDERED that, if the report filed under this Order permits entry of the
scheduling order without a conference, the Court may enter the scheduling order and vacate the
scheduling conference; and it is
FURTHER ORDERED that, except as expressly stated in this Order, the timing of initial
disclosures under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(a)(1)(C) and the timing and extent of
discovery remain governed by the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, the Local Civil Rules, and the
2

operative orders of this Court. This Order does not create, extend, or lift any restriction on
disclosures or discovery. Any additional restriction pending the scheduling conference must be
imposed by an express order identifying its scope and the date or event on which it ends; and it is
FURTHER ORDERED that, within seven (7) days after the scheduling conference, or after
receipt of a report that permits entry of the scheduling order without a conference, the Court will
enter either (a) a scheduling order under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 16(b)(3), or (b) an interim
case-management order identifying the step that remains before the complete scheduling order can
be entered, the basis for deferring its completion, the case-management directions established at
the conference, and the date or event on which the complete scheduling order will be addressed.
An interim case-management order under clause (b) is not a scheduling order under Rule 16(b)(3)
unless it contains the limits that Rule 16(b)(3)(A) requires; and it is
FURTHER ORDERED that, except as expressly stated in this Order, this Order does not
modify any other order of the Court and does not resolve any objection or motion pending before
the District Judge.
The Clerk's Office is directed to provide a copy of this Order to pro se Plaintiff at his last
known address.
It is SO ORDERED.
Alexandria, Virginia
_ 2026
William E. Fitzpatrick
United States Magistrate Judge
